 # Core
 
-Extendable framework with geometric functionality, renderer, etc.
+Extendable spatial framework around persistent topology, runtime execution, and rendering.
 
 # Extension
 
-Extensions are data-only. They dont contain any executable code.
+An extension is a data-only namespace packaged by `extension.json`. It groups declarative assets such as actions, interactions, views, attributes, and properties. Extensions do not ship executable code; the runtime interprets their data against predefined capabilities.
 
 Everything below this section is part of an extension.
 
 ## Action
 
-An action is a headless operation exposed by an extension. Actions mutate or derive spatial data without defining renderer behavior. All calls to geometric operations happens over a predefined set of functions and special variables accessible.
+An action is a declarative headless operation document. It describes how the runtime reads, writes, derives, or transforms spatial data by invoking predefined capabilities and variables.
 
 ## Interaction
 
-An interaction is a renderer-facing state machine exposed by an extension. It gathers input, previews intent, and usually resolves into one or more actions.
+An interaction is a declarative static state machine for the renderer. It describes prompts, picks, transient state, previews, and transitions that usually resolve into one or more actions.
 
 ## Model
 
-A model is the root document for spatial data. It stores objects, their topology references, and the extension data attached to them.
+A model is the root spatial document. It contains objects, their extension data, and references into shared topology.
 
 ## Topology
 
-Topology is the persistent geometric core. It stores the connected spatial graph that objects and derived views reference.
+Topology is the persistent geometric core. It stores connected spatial relationships independently from extension-specific semantics.
 
 ## Object
 
-An object is a node in the model that binds extension data to topology. Objects can form hierarchies and can contribute to derived views.
+An object is an addressable carrier of extension data inside a model. It may reference topology and child objects, but it has no built-in class system; concepts such as typology are extension-defined data rather than core semantics.
 
 ## View
 
-A view is a computed perspective on a model. Views derive objects from source objects, preserve traceability back to their sources, and can attach their own extension data.
+A view is an extension-defined derived context over a model. It may derive view objects from source objects, preserve source links, and own its own subordinate extension assets such as actions, interactions, attributes, and properties.
 
 ## Attribute
 
-An attribute is extension data attached to topology or objects. Attributes describe authored metadata rather than derived results.
+An attribute is attached extension data. It constrains or describes topology, objects, or view-local objects without being a derived result.
 
 ## Property
 
-A property is extension data derived from geometry, topology, objects, or views. Properties describe computed results and should be reproducible from source data.
+A property is computed extension data. It declares a derived result and its source domain rather than authored metadata.
 
-All concrete actions, interactions, views, attributes, and properties live as JSON extension assets under `spatial/assets/extension`.
+All concrete actions, interactions, views, attributes, and properties live as JSON extension assets under `spatial/assets/extension`. Each extension has `extension.json`; each view lives in a `<view-id>/view.json` folder so it can later own its own assets.
*** End Patch
